book_meta.work: The Seven Voyages of Sindbad, from ألف ليلة وليلة
book_meta.author: traditional

sentences.ar: فكيت الحبال، ووقفت، وما شفت إشي.
sentences.en: I undid the ropes, stood up, and saw nothing.

sentences.ar: عتمة كاملة، وريحة موت، وصوت مي بتنقط من بعيد.
sentences.en: Complete darkness, the smell of death, and the sound of water dripping far off.

sentences.ar: مشيت وإيدي قدامي، ودعست على عظام.
sentences.en: I walked with my hands before me, and stepped on bones.

sentences.ar: كانت المغارة كبيرة، وفيها كل الموتى من مية سنة.
sentences.en: The cave was big, with all the dead of a hundred years in it.

sentences.ar: قعدت بزاوية، وأكلت خبزة وحدة، وشربت شوي.
sentences.en: I sat in a corner, ate one loaf, and drank a little.

sentences.ar: وقلت: سبع خبزات، سبع أيام.
sentences.en: And I said: seven loaves, seven days.

sentences.ar: وبعدين بموت.
sentences.en: And then I die.

sentences.ar: وبعد أيام، سمعت الحجر بينشال.
sentences.en: And after days, I heard the stone being lifted.

sentences.ar: ونزل ضو، وصندوق، ووراه واحد بيبكي.
sentences.en: And light came down, and a coffin, and after it someone weeping.

sentences.ar: رجل نزلوه مع مرته الميتة، ومعه خبزه وميته.
sentences.en: A man they had lowered with his dead wife, with his bread and water.

sentences.ar: ورجع الحجر، ورجعت العتمة.
sentences.en: And the stone went back, and the darkness returned.

sentences.ar: ومشيت عليه بالعتمة، وأخدت خبزه وميته.
sentences.en: And I went to him in the darkness, and took his bread and water.

sentences.ar: ما بدي أحكي لك كيف.
sentences.en: I do not want to tell you how.

sentences.ar: قال الحمّال: ما بدي أعرف.
sentences.en: The porter said: I do not want to know.

sentences.ar: قال السندباد: الجوع بيخلي الإنسان إشي تاني.
sentences.en: Sindbad said: hunger makes a person into something else.

sentences.ar: وأنا عشت، وهو ما عاش.
sentences.en: And I lived, and he did not.

sentences.ar: وضليت هيك شهور.
sentences.en: And I stayed like that for months.

sentences.ar: كل ما ينزلوا واحد، آخد أكله.
sentences.en: Every time they lowered one, I took his food.

sentences.ar: وبيوم، سمعت صوت مش من فوق.
sentences.en: And one day, I heard a sound not from above.

sentences.ar: صوت تنفس، وأقدام زغيرة، من جوا المغارة.
sentences.en: The sound of breathing, and small feet, from inside the cave.

sentences.ar: حيوان.
sentences.en: An animal.

sentences.ar: إجا ياكل من الموتى، وشافني، وهرب.
sentences.en: It had come to eat from the dead, saw me, and fled.

sentences.ar: وفكرت: من وين فات؟
sentences.en: And I thought: where did it come in from?

sentences.ar: ومشيت وراه بالعتمة، بين العظام، ساعات.
sentences.en: And I followed it in the dark, among the bones, for hours.

sentences.ar: لحد ما شفت نقطة ضو.
sentences.en: Until I saw a point of light.

sentences.ar: كان شق بالصخر، بيطلع عالبحر.
sentences.en: It was a crack in the rock, opening onto the sea.

sentences.ar: زحفت فيه، وطلعت، وشفت الشمس، وبكيت.
sentences.en: I crawled through it, came out, saw the sun, and wept.

sentences.ar: وبعدين رجعت عالمغارة.
sentences.en: And then I went back into the cave.

sentences.ar: قال الحمّال: رجعت؟!
sentences.en: The porter said: you went back?!

sentences.ar: قال السندباد: رجعت.
sentences.en: Sindbad said: I went back.

sentences.ar: لأنه كل ميت نزلوه، نزلوا معه ذهبه ومجوهراته.
sentences.en: Because every dead person they lowered, they lowered his gold and jewels with him.

sentences.ar: وجمعت من المغارة أكتر مما جمعت من كل رحلاتي.
sentences.en: And I gathered from the cave more than I had gathered from all my voyages.

sentences.ar: وقعدت عالشط، عند الشق، أيام، لحد ما مرت سفينة.
sentences.en: And I sat on the shore, by the crack, for days, until a ship passed.

sentences.ar: وقلت لهم: أنا تاجر غرقت سفينتي.
sentences.en: And I told them: I am a merchant whose ship sank.

sentences.ar: وما حكيت عن المغارة.
sentences.en: And I said nothing of the cave.

sentences.ar: ورجعت على بغداد، ومعي ذهب الموتى.
sentences.en: And I returned to Baghdad, with the gold of the dead.

sentences.ar: وأعطى السندباد الحمّال مية دينار، وما ضحك تلك الليلة.
sentences.en: And Sindbad gave the porter a hundred dinars, and did not laugh that night.
